title: Backlog Kintsugi: Prioritization Lab & Micro-cut Playbook
content:
Context:
Quick lab doc for a lightweight, pragmatic approach to two goals: 1) shrink the console backlogs enough to have a coherent sprint surface for next two cycles, and 2) validate a micro-cut technique we can repeat across other product lanes. Tone = workshop notes / decisions + questions to land in followups.

Objective:
- Create a repeatable triage flow that converts ~40 candidate items into a prioritized sprint-ready slice (capacity for 6 devs : 20 story-points) within 90 minutes of group review.
- Produce a 'cutlist' that documents what we drop, what we defer, and what we shallow-scope into a small experiment.

Quick constraints and guardrails:
- Customer-impact first: any item touching an active enterprise onboarding or SLA path gets "protect" unless there's a compensating mitigation.
- Latency/telemetry work trumps cosmetic polish when it unlocks observability for ops.
- Console changes that require infra migration (schema or major api) are medium risk: prefer canary-only or docs-only for this sprint.

Heuristic scoring (used by group during lab)
- Customer Impact (C) : 0–3 (3 = blocking for paying customers)
- Developer / Ops Save (D) : 0–2 (2 = removes large toil)
- Implementation Size (S) : 0–3 (3 = large; higher is worse)
- Strategic value (V) : 0–2 (2 = aligns with roadmap OKR)
Priority score = (C + D + V) - S  // we use integer bins, sort desc

Workshop cadence (90 minutes)
- 00–10m: goal + alignment, quick read of candidate list
- 10–35m: lightning review (2–3 min each) with live scoring in sheet
- 35–60m: cluster by pattern (UX, infra, rollout controls, billing) and identify 6 candidates for micro-cut exploration
- 60–80m: draft sprint slices for top 3, decide fall-through routing for rest (defer / backlog / lower triage)
- 80–90m: capture decision log + owners + followups

Candidate items (short form, taken from backlog dump; IDs are internal JIRA keys)
- INF-3121: Route override UI for canary/rollouts — add "force-region" toggle UI + audit trail. (Notes: enterprise ask; needs backend audit event)
- INF-3180: Token cost breakdown per request in console trace panel (notes: medium complexity; high user value for devs)
- INF-3299: Add TTL to cached prefix entries in Optimize panel (notes: low UI work, infra touches)
- INF-3344: Mobile preview for small-screen console — visual tech debt (notes: low impact, high QA matrix)
- INF-3400: Batch-configuration UX: expose "max latency" slider (notes: quick win if client libs compatible)
- INF-3477: Console users & roles audit export (CSV) (notes: compliance ask from two customers)
- INF-3502: Inline evals runner: allow small prompts run against a saved promptset (notes: prototype in repo)
- INF-3566: Tracing breadcrumb for fallback model routing (notes: ties to reliability OKR)

Live scoring summary (group quick scores; values are illustrative)
- INF-3121 (C=3 D=1 V=2 S=2) => score = 4  (protect / high)
- INF-3180 (C=2 D=1 V=2 S=2) => score = 3  (target top slice)
- INF-3400 (C=1 D=1 V=1 S=1) => score = 2  (quick win)
- INF-3477 (C=3 D=0 V=1 S=2) => score = 2  (compliance -> schedule near-term)
- INF-3502 (C=1 D=2 V=2 S=3) => score = 2  (experiment; may be large)
- INF-3566 (C=2 D=1 V=2 S=2) => score = 3  (tie with 3180)

Clustering & cut decisions (output of 35–60m cluster work)
- Cluster A: "Observability + Billing" -> {INF-3180, INF-3566, INF-3121}
  - Decision: take INF-3180 + narrow INF-3566 to "add breadcrumb only to model-fallback path"; defer full routing trace to next sprint. INF-3121 needs backend audit event — move to dedicated infra ticket (protect).
- Cluster B: "Small UX wins" -> {INF-3400, INF-3344}
  - Decision: INF-3400 scoped to UI-only slider + validation (1 dev, 3 pts). INF-3344 deprioritized (high QA cost) -> put in grooming queue for Q1.
- Cluster C: "Security / Compliance" -> {INF-3477}
  - Decision: schedule as canonical compliance spike with CS + Legal; scope as export-only first pass (2 devs, 4 pts)
- Cluster D: "Experiments" -> {INF-3502}
  - Decision: convert to a 1-week spike run by UX+ML engineer; do not block sprint capacity.

Resulting Sprint Cutlist (assumes capacity = 20 pts; target 80% utilization)
- Sprint slice A (10 pts): INF-3180 (6 pts) + INF-3566 (2 pts narrow slice) + DOC: console-trace-howto (2 pts)
- Sprint slice B (3 pts): INF-3400 UI-only slider (3 pts)
- Buffer / Refinement (4 pts): grooming, QA, small followups
- Out-of-sprint experiments: INF-3502 spike (owners: Sana, Jordan)

Owners & next steps (who does what)
- Elena Park: capture sprint-slice tickets + update INF-3180 with acceptance criteria; ensure telemetry event contract (due 2026-10-08)
- Mateo Alvarez: prototype slider wireframe + small spec (due 2026-10-09)
- Sana Iqbal & Jordan Lee: run INF-3502 spike (deliverables: prototype + success criteria by 2026-10-14)
- Eng infra: create backend task for INF-3121 audit event and estimate (linked INF-3610)

Acceptance criteria (for sprint tickets)
- INF-3180: trace panel shows token breakdown per request for successful and failed responses; sampling at 1% default; telemetry schema v2 compatible; product doc + one screenshot in PR
- INF-3566 (narrow): breadcrumb appears when fallback routing occurs, showing previous model id and reason; sample events sent to tracing; unit test for serialization
- INF-3400: slider persists per-user setting; validation prevents setting that violates server-side SLOs; e2e smoke test

Wireframe & quick UX notes (for handoff)
- Trace panel: vertical split -> left: request list, right: expanded trace detail. Token cost row under header (collapsed by default). Click-to-expand shows per-token table.
- Slider: inline under batch config; label = "max latency (ms)"; tooltip with example; default = 200 ms; advanced link opens modal with batch diagnostics.
- Breadcrumbs: micro-pill under response header; small chevron to open history. Keep to 1 line on narrow layouts.

Known open questions / risks:
- Telemetry cost: exposing per-token breakdown increases observability events; need a sampling plan (Sana to scope).
- Audit event for INF-3121: who owns storage + retention? Legal has retention rules we must follow.
- QA surface: small-screen preview (INF-3344) has many permutations; deprioritized but call out for accessibility team review later.

Followups (short list)
- Create trimmed ticket set and label with "kintsugi-cutlist-2026-10" (Elena)
- Postmortem of technique after two runs: measure time-to-ready and % items pruned (team)
- Add a one-pager to Confluence: link from linked_artifacts above (Elena to author)

Notes to reviewers:
- "This is intentionally lightweight: use it to make quick calls. If anyone wants a different scoring formula call it out but let's not re-open scoring in this session."
- If Legal flags retention or export rules for INF-3477, we will push to a compliance spike and adjust sprint scope.

Minutes excerpt (raw scribbles captured in session):
- "Slide for slider can be 2 states: default + advanced — avoids modal proliferation"
- "Breadcrumb design: consider micro-animations but not in this sprint"
- "Spike for inline evals could reuse saved-prompt modal; avoid building new storage schema"

End of doc.
